Personal Information Banks

A directory of the different types of personal information collected by public bodies while conducting business with or providing services to Albertans.

Overview

The Protection of Privacy Act (POPA) requires all public bodies to create a directory that lists the public body’s personal information banks (PIBs) available to the public for inspection and copying.

The purpose of making this information available is to inform individuals of the types of personal information the Government of Alberta has collected.

A PIB is a collection of personal information that is searchable using an individual’s name or another identifier, such as a contact list, client listing, or a program database. Each PIB entry within the directory describes the type of personal information that is collected and how that personal information is used.

Government of Alberta PIBs

As individuals participate in programs or services offered by the Government of Alberta, personal information about the individuals may be collected to deliver these programs or services. Each Government of Alberta department is required to have a publicly accessible directory of PIB.

PIB entries do not provide direct access to an individual’s records or disclose any personal information about individuals.

PIB entries will be added or deleted as they are identified, scheduled or decommissioned.
